question: Which one of the following is not an example of Metamorphic rock ?
solution:
A rock is any naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter. There are three kinds of rock: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic. Igneous rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
 

 Types of rocks
 Characteristics
 
 

 Igneous rock
 
 
 
• It is formed when molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies.
 
• Igneous rock may form with or without crystallization.
 
• It may be intrusive (plutonic) rocks or extrusive (volcanic) rocks.
 
• For example, Granite, Basalt, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Sedimentary rock
 
 
 
• They originate when particles settle out of water or air, or by precipitation of minerals from water.
 
• They accumulate in layers.
 
• For example, Sandstone, Limestone, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Metamorphic rock
 
 
 
• They are formed when existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure, or reactive fluids, such as hot, mineral-laden water.
 
• For example, Marble, Quartzite, Schist, Slate, etc.
 
 
 
 

*Therefore, it is clear that the Granite is an igneous rock, not a metamorphic rock.*
